doc.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18

title: Practicing on a pad to build the wrists
summary: Cie has no practice pad and they talk about making one from rubber. Williams advises constant practice on a pad with two sticks, whistling the tune, to strengthen the wrists, and talks about drum heads.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: No, I don't have a practice pad. I'd love them, I guess. Make one, maybe, too. We could fix them up.
Hitter tube or something like that.

I thought he... I didn't know he... He rolls nice. Oh, you gotta do this practice. That's all that's in the line of drumming this person. Constant practice is like a man doing that guitar. See them guys with them guitars, they got the practice, they chords. And, of course, while they're playing the melody instrument, you see, they can get in the room and whistle a number in this field for these chords. With a drummer, what you got to do, you got to take a practice pad, two sticks, on that table there. And, like I said, this is your bass drum, your foot, you understand, to the floor. And, all this practice, if you're gonna sit down on the chair to yourself, if you're playing any number like that, you can whistle a little hump something in your mind, and this, make you rolls on that pad, you understand, like you're beating on the drum. Same effect. And that'll break your wrist faster than the drum itself. Yeah. Sure would, I hope I tell you. Yeah. Well, see, because when you go to execute this, you see that this drum here is gonna bring the note out, but that pad might be a little harder to roll, but that's what you want. That's what you want, then, when you get to that. That's what you want. Oh, man, now your wrist will be super for that.
Yeah, because I guess some drums is harder than this one.
Yeah, I got them drums on one, because it's got to dry, cool, and make you stick on the roll easier. Yeah, yeah. I kind of slack off of them, in a way.
